question.text: Effective 1 July 2020, what are the stamp duty rates applicable on (a) ISSUE of units of a Cat I/II AIF at a first close, and (b) TRANSFER of units on the secondary market?

answer.text: Nil on issue and 0.015% on transfer.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the uniform stamp-duty regime effective 1 July 2020: issue of units of an AIF attracts 0.005% (five-thousandths of one percent) and transfer of units attracts 0.015% (fifteen-thousandths of one percent). The Fund pays the duty on behalf of the investors at the time of issuance or transfer. NO stamp duty arises at the time of redemption. The Trap: Option A inflates both rates by a factor of 10. Option C applies a flat 0.1% which is the rate for certain debentures/shares, not AIF units. Option D wrongly exempts issue. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same stamp-duty rates. XIX-A uses it in client onboarding flows. XXI-B (PMS) does not have stamp-duty on the PMS mandate itself but on securities purchased. Remember: this is a Central-government-led uniform regime; States cannot alter it. Manager's Pro-Tip: In your fund's expense ratio modelling, stamp duty on ISSUE is a one-time drag of ~0.005% across LP commitments — trivial but disclose it. On secondary transfers (GP-led restructurings, LP-to-LP transfers), 0.015% can add up — negotiate with the trustee who bears the cost upfront vs bill-back.
